topic: Server cluster hardware comparison and optimization
summary_markdown:
The discussion focused on optimizing the configuration for a server cluster (ch01-ch03) by comparing hardware options. Initial considerations included Intel and Graviton processors, with an interest in memory-optimized (32GB) and CPU-optimized (96-128GB) instances.

Concerns were raised regarding using local SSDs for temporary tables and dictionary caches on superservers. It was suggested that opting for more powerful AMD configurations might be preferable to complex SSD setups. The performance difference between R7a and previous generations (like R6a) was noted, specifically concerning vCPU mapping: R7a instances map every vCPU directly to a physical CPU core without Simultaneous Multi-Threading (SMT), unlike prior generations.

The general consensus leaned toward exploring AMD configurations as a viable alternative for cost savings and stability.
decisions: Explore AMD configurations as an alternative hardware option
Review the performance implications of R7a instances vs. previous generations regarding vCPU mapping (no SMT)
action_items: Investigate cost-effective cluster configuration using AMD processors.
